Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can align internally and move toward a pilot: 

Summary of their needs (per call)
- Workload: real-time transaction enrichment (risk scoring + personalized messages)
- Peak sustained throughput target: ~120 req/s (200k req/day typical; bursts to 250 req/s)
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms end-to-end (ideally 80–100ms)
- Model: 13B open model with ~256 token prompts (avg seq length ~180)
- Data concerns: no permanent data persistence in model store; logs/audit required for compliance

Our initial guidance
- Hosted API: fastest to ship; supports bursty traffic and we can use auto-bursting for spikes, but sustained 120 req/s with p95 <=120ms will be borderline depending on model variant and sequence length. We can often hit this with optimized kernels + KV caching but costs are higher for sustained heavy usage.
- Dedicated: recommended for predictable sustained throughput and tighter latency SLOs. Reserved GPU pools give predictable tail latency, plus you can configure autoscale and reserved burst capacity for occasional peaks.

Action items
1) Alex/Priya: confirm whether the 120 req/s is sustained for more than 1 hour, or mostly short bursts (answer by EOD Thu).
2) Redwood (Aditya): run a targeted benchmark for Alex's typical prompt/seq length on the 13B model and share p50/p95/p99 latency and cost estimates (ETA: 24–48 hours).
3) Redwood (Neha/Dylan): prepare a proposed SOW and pilot plan (we'll include Dedicated sizing options + Hosted fallbacks).

Attachments: I attached our recent Q2 benchmarks (summary) and I'll attach a draft SOW after Aditya posts the benchmark numbers.

Thanks —

Thanks Neha —

Quick answers:
- The 120 req/s is our expected sustained daytime volume for a large region (US east) — we expect it to hold for blocks of 4–6 hours during peak business windows. Bursts up to 250 req/s occur but are short (minutes).
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms is a hard requirement for the UX (below that and we see conversion drops). p99 <= 300ms is preferred.

Hi Alex / team —

Thanks for the clarity. Quick technical readout and recommendation based on similar workloads we've run: 

1) Short answer / recommendation- For sustained 120 req/s with p95 <= 120ms on a 13B model (avg seq ~180), Dedicated reserved capacity is the safest option. It gives consistent tail latency because the GPU pool is isolated and we can optimize kernel selection, quantization, and KV cache usage for your prompt distribution.
- Hybrid pattern (Dedicated steady-state + Hosted overflow) is viable and recommended for cost efficiency to absorb short spikes to 250 req/s.

2) Sizing guidance (rough)
- Baseline: 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent workers with optimized compilation and continuous batching should handle ~100–140 inference req/s for the 13B model at avg seq ~180 with p95 around 80–140ms depending on batching efficiency and prompt variety.
- Recommended pilot: Reserve 2 workers and enable burst pool (hosted overlay) for spikes. If you want more headroom for safety, 3 workers gives comfortable buffer and reduces p95 variability.

3) Warm-up / KV cache
- KV cache priming: warm-up depends on prompt reuse. For high prefix reuse, p95 improves dramatically after the first 10–50 unique prefixes. For FinPay patterns (transactional templates + small variations) we expect warm cache benefits within minutes of steady traffic.
- Keep-alive: Dedicated allows idle keep-alive policies to maintain warm model/gpu state; hosted has shorter idle timeouts. We'll configure longer keep-alives in the Dedicated pilot.

4) Autoscale and fallback
- Autoscale policies: scale on token/sec and queue length; we can configure faster scale-up for rapid bursts but there is a short provisioning window — hence the hosted overlay for immediate bursts.
- Fallback: when Dedicated is saturated, requests can overflow to a hosted variant of the same model (maybe a quantized variant) to preserve availability.

5) Next steps (technical deliverables)
- I'll run a targeted benchmark using your representative prompt set (please send a sanitized sample or sample stats). Expected deliverable: p50/p95/p99 latency numbers, tokens/sec cost estimate, and recommended Dedicated sizing (ETA: 24–48 hours once we have the samples).
- I'll attach a short benchmark report to the thread and Neha will draft the SOW with the pilot sizing/options.

Regards,
Aditya Rao

Alex / Priya —

Thanks — based on your confirmation and Aditya's guidance, here's the recommendation and immediate next steps: 

Recommendation (pilot)
- Dedicated reserved capacity sized at 2 x A100-80GB-equivalent workers as the pilot baseline. This should meet the 120 req/s sustained target with p95 in the 80–140ms window depending on batching; if you want tighter headroom choose 3 workers.

- Hybrid model: keep Hosted overlay to soak short spikes to 250 req/s. Requests will route to Hosted only when Dedicated reaches auto-configured saturation thresholds.

Deliverables and timeline
- Aditya: final benchmark report (p50/p95/p99 + cost estimate) — ETA EOD Thu (24–48 hrs after we get prompt samples).
- Neha/Dylan: draft SOW and pilot timeline (includes 30-day pilot, success metrics: sustained p95 <= 120ms for 2+ peak windows, integration checklist, audit/logging scope). I'll attach the SOW draft for review once Aditya's numbers are in.
- Legal / Procurement: We'll include standard SOC2 appendix and a cost estimate for both Dedicated-only and Hybrid options.

Next steps for you
1) Please send a small representative sample set (sanitized) or sample stats (avg seq, prompt variance) — this powers the benchmark.
2) If you want the SOW earlier, confirm whether you'd prefer 2-worker or 3-worker baseline for the draft.

I'll also include a DocuSign link in the SOW for a quick pilot authorization once you sign off on sizing.

Thanks — looking forward to the benchmark results and moving to pilot.
